title: 08/02 — Identifier classes (what "redacted identifiers" means)
owner: P7 (injected). P7 already stores identifier_class as an opaque string on the redacted_identifier item kind and in redaction_manifest; this file is the closed list behind that string.
consumer: the gate's redaction step: a redacted_identifier request names one of these class_ids; the gate looks up the class, applies its transform_id from catalogue 03, and records the class in redaction_manifest. The section-8.4 audit record's 'whether values were redacted' is answerable per item because the manifest names the class.

design_anchor.quote: selected excerpts, redacted identifiers, candidate labels, non-sensitive metadata, and evidence references

rules_preamble: **Closed list.** A class_id outside this list is a load error at the injection site, mirroring P7's treatment of its own vocabularies. Adding a class is a revision of this file, reviewed as such.

**An identifier names a person or an instrument; a fact describes the file.** A course code is a fact; a Social Security number is an identifier. The non_members array is as binding as the entries: nothing there may ever be treated as an identifier class, because redacting it would delete the very evidence the dossier exists to carry.

**always_local: true means the value cannot appear in a cloud dossier even redacted** — its transform must be a dropping transform (drop_span, drop_gps), so nothing derived from the value survives into the released payload. The redaction_manifest still records that a drop occurred, which is how the audit record stays able to answer what left the device.
**jurisdiction_dependent: true means R5 owns the value patterns** (shapes, checksums, label wordings per jurisdiction); this file owns only the class, its transform, and its locality.
**Examples are fake.** Every example below is structurally plausible and deliberately not a real person's data.

**Redaction is not extraction.** Catalogue 06 refused personal-data patterns on the extraction side because a finder would write the values into raw_value and context windows. These classes exist on the gate side: the span is located at release time for the purpose of NOT sending it.

This class governs the name's appearance inside RELEASED TEXT of sensitive material, which is the section-8.4 display-facet 'names' concern, not the fact layer

design_cites.quote: Paths, complete extracted text, OCR output, file hashes, image EXIF, GPS, user edits, group memberships, and raw sensitive values should remain local.

entries.notes: GPS is in the always-local set by name, so it can never appear in a dossier even redacted; the class exists because coordinates also occur INSIDE text (a maps screenshot's OCR, a geotagged export's caption), where the always-local item-kind rule alone would not catch them. drop_gps removes the pair entirely — coarsening to a city would be an invented value, and the transform catalogue forbids generalization

facts and candidate labels; ambiguous in ROLE (authoring school vs target), which is a role_split concern, not an identity concern
domain-schema facts; the dossier exists to carry them

non_members.why: candidate_label item kind, already user-visible vocabulary

non_members.value_kind: file paths, complete extracted text, OCR output, file hashes, EXIF blocks, user edits, group memberships
non_members.why: the always-local SET is enforced at the item-kind level by the gate — nothing here is expressible as a releasable item, so no identifier class is needed to redact it; listing them as classes would wrongly imply an excerpt could carry them redacted

non_members.value_kind: protected characteristics (race, religion, orientation, health status as a category, union membership)
non_members.why: refused as a detection vocabulary entirely — see catalogue 01 ref-protected-characteristics-gazetteer and RESEARCH.md NEEDS-JOSEPH; an identifier class here would require exactly the gazetteer the refusal forbids

refused.why: enumerating them would instruct the extractor to look for them (overnight NEEDS-JOSEPH); the question of detect-to-protect vs decline-to-model is Joseph's and stays open

design_cites.quote: a catalogue that enumerated them would be instructing the extractor to look for them

refused.refuses: IP addresses, MAC addresses, device serials as v1 classes
refused.why: real identifiers, but no detector rule or dossier path in v1 locates them, and a class nothing produces is dead vocabulary; add when a rule needs them

uncertain.question: Is an ORGANIZATION name ever an identifier (a therapist's practice name identifies the patient's condition by implication)?
uncertain.both_sides: Treating organizations as identifiers would redact the institution facts dossiers legitimately need (00 names institution as a Finance field). The narrow case — sensitive-by-implication provider names — is real but unresolvable without the characteristic-category decision, so it waits with it.

uncertain.question: financial_account_number uses keep_last_n while government_id_number uses full token replacement — should they agree?
uncertain.both_sides: Statement convention makes trailing digits recognizable and low-risk for accounts; government IDs have no such convention and their tails are higher-entropy identifiers in themselves. Split is deliberate; Joseph may prefer uniformity.
